title: Device code phishing now reaches AI coding agents
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published lab research on 17 November 2026 showing that one phished approval of an attacker-started OAuth device-code request for GitHub Copilot CLI could, depending on settings, let the attacker steer a remotely controllable agent session, plant misleading entries in agent memory, read cloud-synced sessions and access the user's private repositories. Microsoft stresses these are proof-of-concept outcomes, not attacks seen in the wild, and that any device-flow public client can be abused the same way. Defender XDR adds two high-severity detections (preview) for suspected GitHub Copilot device code phishing delivered by email and by Teams.
why: Coding agents now run commands, keep memory and sync sessions, so a device-code approval is no longer just a token: it is a foothold on a developer workstation and the code base. Entra Conditional Access can block device code flow for Entra sign-ins, but GitHub's own device flow is outside Entra CA.
todo: Block device code flow in Entra Conditional Access (Authentication flows condition) for everyone except documented exceptions.
In GitHub Enterprise, review Copilot CLI policies for remote session control, memory and cloud session storage and turn off what you do not need.
Tell developers that a GitHub verification code sent to them by anyone is a red flag, even though the page is genuinely github.com.
Turn on and tune the two Defender XDR detections where you have GitHub connected; they are preview per Microsoft Learn.
effective_note: Research published 17 Nov 2026; Defender detections in preview — per Microsoft.
